question: We can buy company stock at a 15% discount. Should I?
source: proposal Appendix A, on the Tyler 2026 U.S. Compensation & Benefits Summary

fields.name: espp.discount_percent
fields.source_text: a price equal to 85% of the fair market value of Tyler common stock on the purchase date

fields.name: espp.offering_period_months
fields.source_text: At the end of each quarterly offering period

fields.name: espp.max_contribution_percent
fields.source_text: You may contribute 1-15% of your pay

figures.label: Months of service before you can join
Money in per quarterly offering period at 10%
Built-in gain per quarter (buy at 85% of purchase-date price)

must_include: You cannot join yet: the plan requires six months of service (and 20+ hours a week), so with a Jan 4, 2027 start the earliest is about July 2027.
The built-in gain: buying at 85% of the purchase-date price is about a 17.6% return, about $397 per quarter at 10% of pay.
There is no lookback: the price is 85% of the price on the purchase date only.
The summary does not state a holding period; says to check the full plan document instead of assuming none.
The risk of holding your own employer's stock, and a sell-or-hold rule of thumb (sell soon after purchase unless you choose to hold a small share).
Says it comes after the 401(k) match and an emergency fund.
must_not_include: Saying the plan has a lookback, or a 6-month offering period (that is the synthetic guide).

assumptions: Salary and start date are the synthetic offer letter's ($90,000, Jan 4, 2027) until a real (non-identifying) profile is added.
notes: Document: Tyler 2026 U.S. Compensation & Benefits Summary, page 6. Not committed yet.
